items.text: US stocks rose sharply in a holiday-shortened session that closed at 1 p.m. ET. The Dow gained 1.18% to 50,774.94, the S&P 500 1.60% to 7,297.49 and the Nasdaq 2.31% to 24,129.50. Chip stocks led a rebound in technology shares, with the PHLX Semiconductor index up 4.69%. For the week the S&P 500 rose about 5.6% and the Nasdaq about 6.7%. Newly listed Anthropic jumped about 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price after a volatile first week. Brent crude traded near $97 after attacks on Saudi energy sites and tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and futures markets still lean towards a Fed rate rise in December.
items.notes: Closing figures match across JBizNews and Motley Fool. Some secondary sources (mlq.ai) describe it as the S&P's best week since April 2025; I couldn't open them. Oil figures come from The National (thenationalnews.com/business/energy/2026/11/27/oil-set-to-post-weekly-gain...): Brent was $97.49 mid-morning UAE time and on track for a ~7% weekly gain. Anthropic is also relevant to the 'Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations' thread. The WaPo/AP index wrap was blocked.

items.text: US shoppers spent a record $7.1 billion online on Thanksgiving Day, up 10.4% from a year earlier and above Adobe's $6.9 billion forecast, according to Adobe Analytics figures released on Friday. Adobe expects $12.9 billion in online spending on Black Friday (up 9.2%), $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday and $47.5 billion across Cyber Week. Season-to-date online spending from Nov 1 to 22 topped $82.5 billion, up 9.1%. Mobile devices made up 63.2% of Thanksgiving spending, and Adobe said AI-driven traffic to retail sites rose 162%. Final Black Friday figures were not out at the time of writing.
items.outlet: Pirates & Princesses (citing Adobe Analytics, Seeking Alpha, TipRanks)
items.notes: Link1 is a weak outlet that compiles Adobe data. Link2 (Seeking Alpha) and a Reuters item on US News ('US Black Friday online sales to cross $13 billion, Adobe says', 2026-11-27) appeared in search but I couldn't open them; the Reuters headline rounds to 'over $13bn'. Swap in a Reuters/AP link if one is available. Adobe's numbers are nominal, not inflation-adjusted.

items.text: Hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud platform, Reuters reported in an exclusive citing unnamed sources. Cloud One runs on Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle infrastructure and hosts payroll, maintenance logistics, a munitions-tracking system used at more than 200 sites, and a command-and-control system that processes North American air-defence radar feeds. Sources said the intrusion was found during an upgrade in the past several weeks and that the attackers reached the platform's control layer. In response the Air Force reportedly paused migrations, blocked updates and revoked some administrator rights. Cyber Command is assessing the damage. The Air Force declined to comment on specific systems. It is unknown who the attackers were or whether data was taken.
items.notes: The original is a Reuters exclusive (usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2026-11-27/exclusive-hackers-breach-us-air-force-flagship-cloud-one-computing-platform); I couldn't open it. Reports differ on how many anonymous sources Reuters had: Military.com says five, Forbes says three. The Daily Beast framed it as a blow to Hegseth. Military.com says it could not independently confirm the report. No official confirmation.

items.text: Trump wrote on Truth Social that the US backs Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's efforts to stop oil smuggling, end corruption and bring all weapons under exclusive state control, and that Washington wants a united Iraq that makes its own political decisions. The post came as Baghdad moved to take federal control of Kurdistan Region border crossings and oilfields. Iraq's top court ruled that federal forces can deploy on all borders, which prompted protests in the Kurdish region. Al-Zaidi recently also ordered troops against the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah at Jurf al-Sakhar. Analysts quoted by AFP say the drive fits the US maximum-pressure policy on Iran. A Baghdad dialogue meeting is set for Dec 1.
items.outlet: Al Jazeera (with AFP, Reuters); The National
items.notes: The Truth Social post is primary and both outlets quote it the same way. Al Jazeera stresses the Kurdish protests and the risk of antagonising Iran. The National notes Trump claimed credit for al-Zaidi's premiership and says US troops left Iraq in late September.

items.text: Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Thanksgiving, Trump defended his friendship with Vladimir Putin, saying the goal is to stop the killing and that the main obstacle to peace is that Putin and Zelensky really hate each other. He said he did not know whether Putin would attend the G20 summit in Miami on Dec 14–15, but that Putin certainly can come if he wants. He also played down reports of Russian and Chinese intelligence help to Iran, saying China is very little involved and Russia gives little. In a BBC interview Zelensky called the Trump–Putin friendship strange and said Putin cannot be a friend.
items.notes: E-261127-57 already logged the Truth Social 'pull back' post. What's new here is the remark that Putin can come to the G20 and the comments on Iran's backers. The Iran remarks come from the Times of Israel live blog (timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-27-2026/), which doesn't timestamp them. The Kremlin says no decision on G20 attendance.

items.text: State measles counts kept rising over the holiday week. Minnesota reported 228 cases this year, its most since 1990, with 25 new in the past week, mostly children in Todd County. Wisconsin has at least 918 confirmed cases since August, including at least 88 in the past week, 19 hospitalisations and three deaths this month (two children and an adult in Lafayette County). Officials say 99% of cases were unvaccinated or of unknown status. Ohio has 400 cases in 30 counties, against 45 in all of 2025. The CDC's national count stood at 6,038 cases as of Nov 25.
items.reporter: MPR News Staff; Chad Murphy, James Powel, Mary Walrath-Holdridge (USA TODAY Network)
items.outlet: MPR News; Columbus Dispatch via Yahoo
items.notes: The figures come from state health departments. The national death count is still disputed: the CDC says 9, Reuters' tally of state figures says 14 (see E-261126-09).

items.text: The EPA said its first post-detonation lab results found no lead in 38 public drinking-water samples taken after the Army blew up about five tons of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Nov 25. Its real-time air monitors recorded no detectable airborne lead for 30 hours afterwards. Low lead levels found before the blast at four sites in Illinois and Missouri, all well under the 15 ppb action level, were put down to existing conditions. The EPA has taken more than 3,200 air, water, soil and dust samples and says tap-water, soil and dust results will follow over the coming days.
items.notes: Newsweek covers the air results (from Thursday's EPA update). The 38-sample water result comes only from GSM Global, a low-profile aggregator citing an EPA release of Nov 27. Check against the EPA response page if possible.

items.text: Travel and power were recovering after the Thanksgiving coastal storm. Outages that peaked above 900,000 customers on Thursday evening had roughly halved by Friday afternoon, but several hundred thousand customers from Missouri and Illinois to New Jersey and New York were still without power. More than 1,200 US flights were cancelled on Thanksgiving Day and thousands delayed. Disruption eased on Friday, though delays continued at Boston Logan and New York-area airports. Parts of eastern Missouri got up to 15 inches of snow. Transportation Secretary Duffy had earlier blamed most holiday delays on weather. The FAA expects about 417,000 flights over Nov 23–Dec 1, with the return rush still to come.
items.notes: Both links are from the same lesser-known outlet. I couldn't open any wire or FlightAware/poweroutage.us confirmation. No deaths reported in this source. Domain set to Infrastructure because E-261127-06 already covers the storm itself.

items.text: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was moved from Thursday to Saturday, Nov 28, at 8:30 a.m. because of the coastal storm. Macy's announced the change on Nov 25, and CBS New York says it is the first weather postponement in the parade's history; the only earlier break was the 1942–44 wartime suspension, when helium was needed for the war. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani had warned of gusts up to 65 mph, and Gov. Hochul declared a state of emergency for New York City and nearby counties. Some out-of-town marching bands had trouble staying for the new date.
items.reporter: Jesse Zanger, Marcia Kramer (CBS New York)
items.notes: The decision came on Nov 25 but wasn't in recent_events. The parade takes place after this brief is written. The marching-band detail comes from a CNN headline of Nov 27 that I couldn't open.

items.text: Chief Judge Stephanie Rose of the federal court for the Southern District of Iowa ordered ICE to release Guatemalan immigrant Santos Fredy Perez Recinos from the Polk County Jail within 24 hours. Officers looking for a different man wanted on a state sexual-assault warrant arrested Perez Recinos on Oct 28. After they realised the mistake, the ICE office in Des Moines told them to keep holding him on an immigration warrant. Rose found that re-detaining him without a bond hearing, years after he was released as an unaccompanied minor and with no change in circumstances, violated due process. She called the error almost beyond belief and said such mistakes appear to be increasing.
items.notes: Both links are the same Iowa Capital Dispatch story; the original wouldn't load and KCRG did. The exact ruling date isn't given, only that it came days before Nov 27. Like E-261127-08 (Sabraw), it's part of a pattern of judges limiting re-detention of released immigrants without changed circumstances. Separately and from one source only: Wisevoter, citing Alabama Political Reporter, says the US Attorney in Mobile is appealing Judge Beaverstock's order limiting warrantless construction-site raids to the 11th Circuit (Nov 27). Not logged.

items.text: Andrea Stewart-Cousins, majority leader of the New York State Senate, died on Friday aged 76, her office said, without giving a cause. A senator since 2006, she became leader in 2019, the first woman and first Black woman to lead the chamber. She also chaired the board of the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, Democrats' national arm for state legislative races. She was re-elected on Nov 3 and kept as leader by her conference in mid-November. Gov. Kathy Hochul ordered flags on state buildings flown at half-staff. Succession details are expected in the coming weeks.
items.outlet: AP (via Northern Virginia Daily); WRGB CBS 6 Albany
items.notes: This is state-level news, included because it was national wire copy and her DLCC role is national. Drop if space is tight.

items.text: The comment period on CMS's proposed exchange pre-eligibility verification rule (Working Families Tax Cut Act implementation) closed on Nov 26. The proposal would require verification of eligibility before subsidised marketplace enrolment, starting with 2028 coverage. No final rule or comment tally has been published.
items.notes: Rule R-261026-02 moved from Open for comment to Proposed (comment closed).

items.text: President Karol Nawrocki vetoed the government's PIT/CIT reform on the last day of his 21-day deadline, announcing it in a video. The law would have raised the first PIT threshold from 120,000 to 130,000 zł, added a 24% band up to 150,000 zł, raised the solidarity levy from 4% to 5%, raised CIT from 19% to 22% for firms with revenue above €50m and cut the lump-sum (ryczałt) limit from €2m to €250,000. Nawrocki said it helps a few and takes from most, and criticised the rushed process. Finance Minister Domański said 3.5 million Poles lose a tax cut. Reuters counts it as his 51st veto. Overriding it needs a 3/5 Sejm majority, which the coalition lacks, so 2027 tax rules stay as they are.
items.notes: Also confirmed by money.pl (Malwina Gadawa), Infor, Reuters (via Devdiscourse), Notes from Poland. KO/Lewica (Łoboda, Śmiszek on TVN24) call it a veto for millionaires; Konfederacja (Mentzen) praised it; PiS (Błaszczak) wants a 180,000 zł second threshold instead. egospodarka/finwire: override would fall about 30 votes short; experts see 2028 as the realistic start for any rerun. Domański says he has a 'plan B' (not detailed). Government figure 3.5m beneficiaries disputed by a Palace source (fewer than 3m).

items.text: President Nawrocki vetoed, for the second time, a bill raising the sugar fee on sweetened drinks from January 2027. It would have raised the fixed fee from 50 to 70 grosze per litre, doubled the variable fee to 10 grosze per gram of sugar above 5 g/100 ml, raised the cap from 1.20 to 1.80 zł per litre and lifted the caffeine/taurine fee tenfold to 1 zł per litre. Nawrocki said taxes would exceed 40% of the price of popular drinks and hurt fruit growers, juice makers and small shops. The Health Ministry said the veto costs the NFZ about 1.3bn zł a year for prevention and treatment.
items.notes: Print 3155. He vetoed a similar bill in December 2025.

items.text: Alongside the two vetoes, President Nawrocki signed three laws passed on Nov 5, Infor and Polsat News report. One tightens taxation of family foundations: from 2027 the rate on benefits paid out and on hidden profits rises from 15% to 19%, the CIT exemption for rentals is limited to long-term housing, and assets put in from 2027 must be held two years. A second amends the PIT, CIT and lump-sum acts (print 3137, tax reliefs). The third launches a 4.8bn zł aid programme for energy-intensive firms hit by high electricity prices.
items.notes: Finwire says print 3137 was signed Nov 27 (Chancellery statement 12:54). This is the act already logged as R-261125-02 after earlier, unconfirmed reports of a Nov 18/24 signature. prezydent.pl could not be reached. Family foundations = print 3148; energy-intensive = print 3159.

items.text: The National Prosecutor's Office released findings from an international team of 22 experts (US, UK, Hungary, Denmark, Ireland, Poland), first appointed under PiS in 2019. They say the 2010 Smolensk Tu-154M crash was an accident (controlled flight into terrain) caused by a chain of human errors: a late, too-steep descent in fog and a late go-around, with Russian controllers wrongly confirming the glide path. They found no evidence of an explosion but had no access to the wreckage. Tusk said Kaczyński and Macierewicz should pay a high price for their accusations. PiS figures, including Małgorzata Wassermann and Macierewicz, called it manipulation.
items.notes: Contested: government side vs PiS (Wassermann: unreliable without a site inspection). TVP Info's daily summary confirms the presentation, but only its metadata could be read. Jarosław Kaczyński had not commented by publication.

items.text: Prime Minister Tusk signed orders extending the anti-terrorist alert levels to 23:59 on Feb 28, 2027: BRAVO and BRAVO-CRP nationwide, BRAVO for Polish energy infrastructure abroad, and level three CHARLIE on railway lines run by PKP PLK and PKP LHS. CHARLIE has applied to the railways since the November 2025 sabotage on line 7. Police and the Railway Protection Service will keep patrolling tracks, signalling and stations. The previous orders expired on Nov 30.
items.notes: Neither source mentions Operation Horyzont, the army's support mission, which is a separate presidential/MoD decision.

items.text: The Constitutional Tribunal's disciplinary court, made up of three government-backed judges, suspended Bogdan Święczkowski as Tribunal president for 12 months pending disciplinary proceedings over his refusal to admit five parliament-elected judges whom President Nawrocki has not sworn in. Justice Minister Żurek welcomed the decision. Święczkowski, who did not attend, called the judges usurpers and their decisions legally void. His lawyer said the court was improperly convened.
items.notes: Announced on Nov 26 and reported on Nov 27; not in recent_events. Interia mentions the suspension only in passing. Contested: PiS and the President's camp do not recognise the government-backed judges (the Supreme Court ruled on Nov 19 that only judges sworn in by the president are legitimate).

items.text: Warsaw Mayor Rafał Trzaskowski said the city respects the district court ruling but will appeal it to the Court of Appeal. The ruling overturned the city's ban on continuing the right-wing protest camp in front of the Constitutional Tribunal. A city spokesperson cited resident complaints and negative opinions from the fire service, police and ambulance service about blocking Aleja Szucha for over a month. The organisers have notified an assembly from Nov 30 to Jan 5. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński welcomed the ruling and called supporters to a rally at the Tribunal on Sunday at 15:00.
items.notes: Interia also carries Trzaskowski's statement. The city had 24 hours to file. No date found for the Court of Appeal ruling.

items.text: At about 8:30 on Friday, a Polregio regional train from Kraków entered Katowice Zawodzie station on a track already occupied by a PKP Intercity train from Bohumín to Przemyśl. The regional driver stopped about 200 metres short. PKP PLK blamed a signaller's error in setting the route, and nobody was hurt. Traffic was halted until about 10:00, with shortened routes and mutual ticket acceptance. A commission will investigate.
items.notes: PKP PLK confirmed on the record, quoted by TVN24 (which also cites tarnogorski.info). Affects the Kraków–Katowice line.

items.text: Current and former Żabka franchisees accuse the chain of a misleading model, citing VAT settlements, debts, fee calculations and its control over stores, Rzeczpospolita reports. The BizRescue business forum has filed a crime notice that more than 100 people joined, and has asked the State Labour Inspectorate whether the arrangement amounts to employment. Some franchisees report VAT demands of up to 1.2m zł. Żabka says franchisees are independent businesses responsible for their own taxes, and that seven suits by six former franchisees were pending as of Nov 18.
items.notes: Based on Rzeczpospolita reporting (original paywalled, not opened). Żabka has 13,000+ stores; Couche-Tard takeover offer pending.

items.text: The emergency department of St Barbara Hospital in Sosnowiec admitted its first hypothermia patients of the season after several days of frost, one with a body temperature just under 28°C. Emergency doctor Tomasz Sikora said homeless people, those who cannot afford heating, seniors, small children and people with dementia are most at risk. He urged passers-by to check whether someone lying outside is conscious and to call 112 rather than assume intoxication.
items.notes: PAP is credited. No national hypothermia death figures found.

items.text: Someone sprayed gas, most likely bear spray, in the crowded dining room of the Morskie Oko mountain shelter in the Tatras early on Friday afternoon, PAP reports. All guests were taken outside and the rooms aired, and no one was hurt. Staff called the act irresponsible and said it was the first such incident at the shelter. The perpetrator fled and could not be identified from security footage.
items.notes: Lesser Poland (Tatras). Source is the shelter management, via PAP.

items.text: The parents of the young girl seen in widely shared footage being shot at on ul. Grodzka during the 7 Nov attack have come forward to prosecutors, prosecutor Eryk Stasielak, head of the Małopolska branch of the National Prosecutor's Office, told PAP. The girl was not hit. Prosecutors classify the shots at her as attempted murder, and she and her parents now have the status of injured parties. Prosecutors had first verified the footage, then appealed for the family to come forward. Stasielak gave no further details, citing the family's rights.
items.notes: Also reported by Rzeczpospolita and Niedziela (not opened). The family's identity is withheld. This closes the earlier prosecutors' search for the parents noted in W-261110-02.

items.text: LoveKraków reports new investigative details on the 7 Nov attack from prosecutor Eryk Stasielak. Investigators estimate the attacker kept about 1,000 rounds at home, carried about 500 and fired roughly 100. Police secured two rifles and two pistols; one rifle was used. Four phones (his and three relatives') were seized and data has been extracted from most. He held a permit for ten firearms and his father one for eleven, and how those permits were issued is under review. He was recorded on Aleje Trzech Wieszczów around 15:00 before walking to the Main Square. Autopsy results are still awaited, and Stasielak said all versions, including foreign influence, remain open.
items.notes: Possibly from the same prosecutor briefing as E-261127-26 (PAP, 26 Nov). Only the ammunition, phone, weapons, permit and route details are new here; the 'foreign influence' line is not.

items.text: Mayor Łukasz Gibała announced on social media that the city will give the Kraków police 200,000 zł for bulletproof vests and first-aid rescue kits, at the request of the city police commander. The number of items and the delivery timeline were not given. The decision follows reports that the two officers who stopped the 7 Nov attacker wore privately bought vests. Małopolska police have said concealable vests cover about half of their needs and heavy vests about 24%.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: Based on the mayor's own post, quoted by KR24. krakow.net.pl credits Onet. Linked to W-261120-11 (vest inquiry).

items.text: Firefighters identified the source of the elevated radiation found in waste at the Rydygier Specialist Hospital on 26 Nov as a capsule of iodine-131, an isotope used in cancer therapy. The capsule was put in a shielded container, and the rest of the waste was isolated until radiation falls and sanitary inspectors give further instructions. No contamination was found in hospital staff or at other checked locations, and responders were decontaminated. The operation involved 29 firefighters, eight vehicles, police and the regional sanepid. Neither report says how the capsule got into municipal waste.
items.notes: Both reports rely on State Fire Service (PSP) information. Neither mentions any investigation into how the capsule was disposed of.

items.text: MPK Kraków says PESA has started building the bodies of Kraków's new trams in Bydgoszcz. The order covers 65 vehicles: 30 bidirectional 33 m trams first, initially for the planned Azory line, then 20 single-direction 43 m and 15 bidirectional 33 m trams. MPK wants 25 more under the framework deal if funding allows. MPK president Rafał Świerczyński told Radio Kraków the first tram should arrive in June or July 2027, with homologation taking months. The first 30 would let MPK retire all high-floor, non-air-conditioned trams (220 of 330 trams are low-floor now). The city moved over 82m zł of EU money from the ul. Starowiślna rebuild to the purchase.
items.notes: Sources differ on timing: krakow.net.pl (citing mpk.krakow.pl) says the first tram comes in 2027 for tests and training, with the first contractual delivery in February 2028. LoveKraków says the first tram arrives in June or July 2027. The split of the 35 later trams also differs slightly. Contract value not given.

items.text: The Christmas market on Rynek Główny opened with tighter security after the 7 Nov attack, Radio Kraków reports: more security staff and CCTV cameras, concrete barriers on access roads, a rescuers' medical point in the Sukiennice, and more police and city guard patrols. About 100 kiosks are taking part, with vendors from Poland, Lithuania, Ukraine, Slovakia, the UK and Hungary. A second fair on Mały Rynek runs from 30 Nov to 3 Jan. The residents' group Zabytkowe Centrum criticised the longer hours (to 23:00 on Fridays and Saturdays, alcohol sales to 22:00), saying it means more noise for people living in the centre.
items.notes: No exact numbers for guards, cameras or patrols. The residents' criticism comes from founder Ryszard Rydiger on social media (KRKnews, Małgorzata Armada).

items.text: The agenda for the City Council's 67th session on Wed 2 Dec (11:00) is published on BIP. It includes first readings of the 2027 budget (druk 1642) and the multi-year financial forecast (druk 1641); second reading of the fare resolution (druk 1587, with the Nowa Lewica amendment); the postponed final vote on the Piaski Nowe local plan (druk 1558); municipal housing rental rules (druk 1639); and several 2026 budget changes. KRKnews says budget amendments are due by 7 Dec, the budget committee must respond by 11 Dec, and the budget must pass by 31 Dec. Withdrawal from Eurocities and other associations, honorary citizenship for the two police officers, and the flat-sale consultations are not on the published agenda.
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: KRKnews byline reads Grzegorz Górski; page metadata says Grzegorz Skowron. The agenda can still change at the start of the session. No 2027 budget totals are given in these sources (Krakowski Raport earlier gave a deficit of 956.9m zł).

items.text: Public consultation on the draft resolution shrinking the Clean Transport Zone (SCT) opened on 27 Nov and runs to 18 Dec. The zone would shrink from about 196 km² to about 1 km² inside the first ring road. Residents' cars held by end-2028 would be exempt, actual residence plus paying PIT in Kraków would replace registration, and stickers would be replaced by number-plate checks. Public meetings are on 3 Dec (Nowa Huta, ARTzona), 7 Dec (Rynek Podgórski 1), 10 Dec (XIV LO, ul. Chełmońskiego) and 17 Dec (pl. Wszystkich Świętych), all 17:00–19:00. The separate consultation on freezing SCT fees for 2027–2028 closed the same day.
items.notes: Official source only. The page is unclear on whether only electronic forms count up to the end of 18 Dec. Emission standards and fee rates stay the same. Current rules apply until 30 days after the new resolution is published in the regional journal.

items.text: Kraków City Hall has made public its appeal against the Małopolska voivode's decision (No. 1/2026 of 21 Oct) approving the UKEN university shooting-range complex at ul. Rydla 54 in Bronowice, near Fort 7. The appeal was filed on 10 Nov by the head of the city's green-space authority ZZM and goes to the Minister of Finance and Economy. The city says over 270 trees would be felled and objects to the decision's immediate enforceability. It also questions whether classrooms, garages and parking fall under the special act for universities. The city was not recognised as a party and is also seeking that status. No appeal proceedings have been opened yet.
items.notes: The appeal was filed on 10 Nov but announced by the city (krakow.pl) on 27 Nov. Dziennik Polski also covered it (not opened, site error). Linked to W-261123-05.

items.text: Kraków will not use a roughly 175,000 zł grant from the sports ministry's pilot 'Szatnia na medal' programme to renovate changing rooms at the ice rink at ul. Siedleckiego 7, LoveKraków reports. The only bid in the city sports-infrastructure board (ZIS) tender was 430,000 zł, about 175,000 zł over the planned budget, so the tender was cancelled. The ministry refused to extend the deadline or pay out the grant, and the agreement was dissolved by mutual consent on 25 Nov. Planned work covered eight rooms of over 400 m², including four players' changing rooms.
items.notes: ZIS spokesman Sławomir Farbaniec confirmed the refusals and the dissolution.

items.text: Johannes Vermeer's 'Young Woman with a Pearl Necklace' (1663/65), on loan from Berlin's Gemäldegalerie, is on show at Wawel Royal Castle until 28 February 2027. It is the first time the painting has been shown in Poland. Because of conservation requirements, no more than 20 visitors may be in the room at once. November entry to Wawel exhibitions is free with a timed ticket, reserved online up to a week ahead.
items.notes: Krakowportal confirms the Vermeer display and the free November tickets.

items.text: Public consultation on the draft resolution freezing Clean Transport Zone (SCT) entry fees for 2027–2028 closed on 27 Nov. The draft now awaits a City Council vote and is not on the 2 Dec session agenda; consultation results have not yet been published.
items.notes: Rule R-261106-06 moved from Open for comment to Proposed.
